headline: AI FOUND **PHP**
BUGS: SITES DOWN
cover.hook_pick_reason: Names PHP and says AI found the bugs, fixing the old 'AI flaws' wording that read as flaws in AI. States the event the slides prove: sites (government portals, hospitals, a port, universities) went offline in Europe. The number hook ('holes in 70% of web') overstates: 70% is PHP's share of sites, not how many are affected. The reader-impact hook is supported but 'sites you use' is looser than the article. The myth-flip hook is a framing, not the news.
cover.image_prompt: Cinematic wide shot of a dark control room wall of glowing server racks and screens, most going dark one by one down a long corridor, a single cracked line of amber light running through the central rack like a fault line, cool blue haze, shallow depth of field. Main subject in the upper half, lower third in deep shadow. No text, no letters, no logos, no people.

slides.title: Sites went dark across Europe
body: In the Netherlands, government portals, the **Port of Rotterdam**, the football association and several hospitals took public websites offline. Germany's University of Freiburg and Austria's University of Vienna paused some systems. AI Times reports some were precautions.

slides.title: Two holes hiding since 2004
body: The US National Security Agency (NSA) warned of two critical holes in PHP, software behind roughly **70%** of websites. They sit in every version since PHP 5 (2004). Called PHP2Shell, each scored **9.2 out of 10** for severity.

slides.title: AI found them
body: Security firm Calif found one flaw with GPT-5.6 Sol in OpenAI's "Patch the Planet" initiative. Wiz, a security firm owned by Google, used its AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. One Wiz researcher did in **a week** what top teams need months for.

slides.quote: With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts.

slides.title: Attack attempts, damage unclear
body: OpenAI says researchers found the flaws **before hackers**. Cloudflare saw initial attack attempts; the scale of any intrusions or leaks is not yet confirmed. The NSA advises pulling unpatchable PHP sites offline. Censys counted **1.5M** of about 2.6M hosts on hard-to-fix versions.

facts.text: The US National Security Agency warned that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation.
PHP powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet, by some accounts more than 33 million sites.
The holes have been in all versions of PHP since version 5, released in 2004.
Security firm Calif, working in OpenAI's 'Patch the Planet' initiative, found one flaw using GPT-5.6 Sol; Wiz used its AI agent, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol to find multiple vulnerabilities.
The NSA's guidance is that a PHP site that cannot be patched right away should be pulled offline until it can be.
Wiz warned: 'With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts.'

OpenAI says the flaws were found by researchers before hackers. TechCrunch reported no reports of exploits in the wild at publication; AI Times says the scale of actual intrusions or data leaks has not yet been confirmed.

In the Netherlands, government portals, the Port of Rotterdam, the football association, major political parties and several hospitals took public websites offline; Germany's University of Freiburg, Austria's University of Vienna, the Wikimedia Foundation and the Internet Archive also paused some sites or systems.
Wiz said one researcher finished in a week what a world-class team would have needed months for; the two flaws are called 'PHP2Shell' and each scored 9.2 out of 10 for severity.
Censys observed about 2.6 million hosts, of which 1.5 million ran PHP versions that cannot easily receive the fix.
Cloudflare said it already observed some initial attack attempts and added protections for customers.
AI Times reports that some of the site shutdowns were precautionary measures (예방 조치).

caption:
PHP, the software behind roughly 70% of websites, just had two critical flaws found with AI, and sites went offline across Europe, some as a precaution.

The US National Security Agency (NSA) warned of the holes, which sit in every PHP version since 2004. Dutch government portals, hospitals and the Port of Rotterdam took public sites offline.

→ Each flaw scored 9.2 out of 10 for severity
→ Wiz says one researcher did in a week what a top team needs months for
→ OpenAI says researchers found them before hackers; Cloudflare saw early attack attempts, and the scale of any damage is not yet confirmed

Should old code be re-audited with AI before attackers do it?

Source: TechCrunch, "PHP Armageddon: OpenAI, Google's Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet", Oct 21, 2026; AI Times, "웹사이트 70% 쓰는 PHP서 AI가 결함 발견…각국 정부 사이트 중단", Oct 22, 2026.
